paragraphs: Art. 8. A contract is an agreement between two or more persons to create, regulate or dissolve a legal relationship between them.
Persons exercise their rights to satisfy their interests. They may not exercise these rights contrary to the interests of society.
Art. 9. The parties may freely determine the content of the contract as far as it does not contradict the mandatory rules of the law and good morals.
Art. 12. In negotiating and concluding contracts the parties must act in good faith. Otherwise they owe damages.
Art. 14. A contract is deemed concluded when the acceptance reaches the offeror.
If after the acceptance is sent one of the parties dies or falls into a state that is a ground for judicial disability, the contract is deemed concluded.
The contract is deemed concluded at the place where the offer was made.
Art. 17. If the parties hide their real agreement behind a sham agreement, the rules on the hidden agreement apply if the conditions for its validity are met.
Rights that third persons acquired in good faith from the acquirer under the sham agreement are preserved, except rights in real estate acquired after the entry of the claim to establish the sham.
This rule also applies to creditors of the acquirer under the sham agreement who imposed an attachment or distraint on its object.
Art. 18. Contracts for the transfer of ownership or the creation of other real rights in real estate must be made by notarial deed.
Art. 19. A preliminary contract for the conclusion of a final contract that requires notarial or notarially certified form must be made in writing.
The preliminary contract must contain agreements on the essential terms of the final contract.
Either party to the preliminary contract may sue for the conclusion of the final contract. In that case the contract is deemed concluded when the court decision becomes final.
Art. 26. Contracts that contradict or circumvent the law, and contracts that offend good morals, including contracts on inheritances not yet opened, are void.
Contracts with an impossible object, contracts without consent, without the form prescribed by law or without a cause, and sham contracts are also void. The cause is presumed until proven otherwise.

The nullity of separate parts does not make the contract void when they are replaced by mandatory rules of law or when it can be presumed that the transaction would have been concluded without the invalid parts.

Art. 27. Contracts concluded by persons without capacity, or by their representative without observing the requirements set for them, and contracts concluded by mistake, fraud, threat or extreme necessity are voidable.
Art. 30. A threat is a ground for annulment of a contract when one party was forced by the other party or by a third person to conclude it by arousing a justified fear.
Art. 31. A contract concluded by a person with capacity is voidable if at its conclusion the person could not understand or control his acts.
The annulment of such a contract cannot be sought after the person's death, unless judicial disability was requested before the death or the proof of incapacity arises from the contract itself.
Art. 32. Only the party in whose interest the law allows voidability may seek annulment.

The right to seek annulment expires after three years. The term runs from the day the person came of age, the disability was lifted, the mistake or fraud was discovered or the threat ended, and in other cases from the day of the contract.
A defendant sued for performance of a voidable contract may seek annulment by objection even after the term has expired.
Art. 34. When a contract is declared void or annulled, each party must return to the other everything it received from it.
Art. 35. A voidable contract may be confirmed by the party entitled to seek annulment, by a written act that also states the ground of voidability.
The contract is also confirmed when that party performs it voluntarily, wholly or partly, knowing the ground of voidability.
A contract voidable for extreme necessity cannot be confirmed.
Art. 36. A person may represent another by provision of law or by the will of the represented person.
The effects of the legal acts performed by the representative arise directly for the represented person.

Art. 37. An authorisation to conclude contracts for which the law requires a special form must be given in the same form; but if the contract must be concluded in notarial form, the authorisation may also be given in writing with notarial certification of the signature and the content made at the same time.
Art. 38. A representative may not contract in the name of the represented person with himself or with another person he also represents, unless the represented person consented.
The principal always has the right to revoke the authorisation, and the agent to renounce it. A waiver of this right by the principal or the agent is invalid.
Art. 39. The scope of the agent's power towards third persons is determined by what the principal stated.
When several persons are authorised for an act, each of them may perform it alone, unless the authorisation provides otherwise.
Art. 40. If the representative and the person with whom he contracts agree to the detriment of the represented person, the contract has no effect for the represented person.

Art. 41. The authorisation ends with its revocation or renunciation, with the death or judicial disability of the principal or the agent, and when the principal or agent is a legal entity, with its termination.
The end of the authorisation cannot be relied upon against third persons who contracted with the agent in good faith, unless the end was subject to entry and was entered.
Art. 42. A person who acted as a representative without power of representation owes damages to the other party if that party was in good faith.
The person in whose name a contract was concluded without power may confirm it. The confirmation requires the same form as the authorisation to conclude the contract.
Art. 43. The agent may re-delegate to another person if authorised to do so or if the re-delegation became necessary to protect the principal's interests.
The re-delegation may be revoked by the principal and by the delegating agent.

The agent must immediately inform the principal of the re-delegation and give him the necessary information about the sub-agent. If the agent fails to do so, he answers for the sub-agent's acts as for his own.
Art. 44. The rules on contracts apply accordingly to unilateral statements of will in the cases where the law allows them to create, change or end rights and obligations.

Art. 87. When the debtor under a bilateral contract fails to perform for a reason for which he is responsible, the creditor may terminate the contract by giving the debtor a reasonable term for performance with a warning that after the term he will consider the contract terminated. The warning must be in writing when the contract is in writing.

The creditor may declare termination without giving a term if performance has become wholly or partly impossible, if because of the debtor's delay it has become useless, or if the obligation had to be performed strictly at the agreed time.

Contracts that transfer, create, recognise or end real rights in real estate are terminated through the court. If the defendant offers performance during the proceedings, the court may give a term for it according to the circumstances.
Termination is not allowed when the unperformed part of the obligation is insignificant for the creditor's interest.
The right to terminate the contract expires after five years.

Art. 92. A penalty secures the performance of the obligation and serves as compensation for the damage from non-performance, without the damage having to be proved. The creditor may also claim compensation for greater damage.
If the penalty is excessive compared to the damage suffered, or if the obligation was performed improperly or partly, the court may reduce it.
Art. 93. Earnest money serves as proof that the contract was concluded and secures its performance.

If the party who gave the earnest money does not perform, the other party may withdraw from the contract and keep the earnest money. If the party who received it does not perform, the other party, on withdrawing from the contract, may claim double the earnest money.
If the party not at fault prefers to claim performance, damages are determined under the general rules.
Art. 99. The creditor may assign his claim, unless the law, the contract or the nature of the claim prevents this.
The assigned claim passes to the new creditor with its privileges, securities and other accessories, including accrued interest, unless agreed otherwise.
The former creditor must notify the debtor of the assignment, hand to the new creditor the documents establishing the claim and confirm the assignment in writing.
The assignment takes effect towards third persons and the debtor from the day the former creditor notifies the debtor.
Art. 110. All claims for which the law does not provide another term expire after five years.
Art. 111. The following claims expire after three years:
a) claims for remuneration for work, unless another term is provided;
b) claims for damages and penalties from an unperformed contract;
c) claims for rent, interest and other periodic payments.
d) (Repealed.)

Art. 135. A creditor may ask that acts by which the debtor damages him be declared ineffective towards him, if the debtor knew of the damage when performing them. When the act is for value, the person with whom the debtor contracted must also have known of the damage. The ineffectiveness does not affect rights acquired for value by third persons in good faith before the entry of the claim.
Knowledge is presumed until proven otherwise if the third person is the debtor's spouse, descendant, ascendant, brother or sister.
When the act was performed before the claim arose, it is ineffective only if the debtor and the person with whom he contracted intended to damage the creditor.

The creditors in whose favour the ineffectiveness is declared are satisfied from the proceeds of the public sale before the third person, when the latter takes part in the distribution with a claim arising from the declaration of ineffectiveness.
Art. 149. To secure a claim, a pledge over a movable thing or a claim, and a mortgage over real estate, may be created.
A pledge and a mortgage may be created for one's own and for another person's obligation.

Art. 152. An agreement made in advance that the creditor will become the owner of the thing if the obligation is not performed, and any other agreement made in advance on a way of satisfying the creditor different from the one provided by law, is invalid.
Art. 166. A mortgage is created by entry in the property register, made on the basis of a contract or of the law.
It may be created only on individually identified properties and for a fixed sum of money.
Art. 167. The mortgage contract is concluded by notarial deed.

It states: the full names, residence and occupation of the creditor and of the debtor, and of the owner of the property if the mortgage secures another person's obligation, and for a legal entity its exact name; the property mortgaged; the secured claim, its maturity and the interest if agreed, and the sum for which the mortgage is created if the claim is not for money.
A mortgage may be created only on properties that, at the conclusion of the contract, belong to the person who creates it.
Art. 168. A statutory mortgage is created:
1. in favour of the transferor of real estate – on the property transferred, to secure his claims under the contract; and
2. in favour of a co-sharer owed an equalisation of his share – on the real estate allotted to the co-sharer who owes it.
The statutory mortgage is entered on the creditor's request, with a copy of the act of transfer or partition attached. The request must contain all data under Art. 167(2).
Art. 169. The mortgage ranks from its entry.

Art. 170. The creation of a mortgage is invalid if the mortgage contract, the request for a statutory mortgage or the act on which it is based leaves uncertain the identity of the creditor, the owner or the debtor, the identity of the property and of the secured claim, or the sum for which the mortgage is created.

Art. 171. To have effect, the transfer and pledge of a claim secured by a mortgage, subrogation into it, its attachment, and the novation and substitution of a debtor in an obligation secured by a mortgage must be made in writing with notarially certified signatures and entered in the property register.
Art. 172. The effect of the entry lasts 10 years from the day it is made. It may be extended if the entry is renewed before the term expires.
If the term expires without renewal, the mortgage may be entered again. In that case it ranks from the new entry.
The entry is renewed on a request with a copy of the contract or of the request for the mortgage.
Art. 173. A creditor whose claim is secured by a mortgage has the right to be satisfied with priority from the price of the mortgaged property, whoever owns it.
The right of priority also extends to the income from the property from the day on which, in enforcement, the owner must account for it under the Civil Procedure Code.

If the claim is for a fixed sum of money, or a money penalty was agreed for it, the creditor may ask for an order for immediate enforcement under Art. 418 of the Civil Procedure Code on the basis of the act of entry of the mortgage.
Art. 179. The entry of a mortgage is deleted on the creditor's consent, which must be given in notarially certified form, or on a final court decision.
The deletion is made on a request with the act of consent or a copy of the final decision attached. It is made by a note in the file of the mortgaged property.
The deletion extinguishes the mortgage. But if the act on which the deletion was made is declared invalid, the mortgage may be entered again. In that case it ranks from the new entry.
Art. 183. By a contract of sale the seller undertakes to transfer to the buyer the ownership of a thing or another right against a price that the buyer undertakes to pay.

Art. 186. The costs of the contract and other expenses connected with the transfer of ownership are borne by the buyer, except in the sale of real estate, where the costs are paid by the parties equally.
The costs of delivery, including measuring and weighing, are borne by the seller, and the costs of acceptance by the buyer.
Art. 188. The seller is liable if third persons have ownership or other rights in the thing that they can assert against the buyer, unless the buyer knew of them.
Art. 193. The seller is liable if the thing sold has defects that substantially reduce its price or its fitness for ordinary use or the use provided in the contract.
The seller is not liable for defects known to the buyer at the sale.
The seller is liable even when he did not know of the defect. An agreement excluding liability is invalid.

Art. 197. The buyer's claims under Art. 195 expire after one year in the sale of real estate and after six months in the sale of movables. If the seller knowingly concealed the defect, the term is three years. The parties may extend or shorten the term by agreement.
The term runs from the handover of the thing.
Art. 223. The rules on sale apply accordingly to exchange; each party is considered the seller of what it gives and the buyer of what it receives.
Art. 225. By a contract of gift the donor gives a thing at once and free of charge to the recipient, who accepts it.
A gift of movables must be made in writing with notarially certified signatures or by handover, and a gift of securities in the manner required for their transfer.
Art. 226. A promise of a gift has no effect.
A gift is void as far as it concerns future property.
A gift is also void when it, or the only motive for which it was made, is contrary to the law or good morals, and when its conditions or burden are impossible.
Art. 227. A gift may be revoked when the recipient:
a) intentionally kills or attempts to kill the donor, the donor's spouse or child, or is an accomplice in such a crime, unless the act was committed in circumstances that exclude punishability;
b) falsely accuses the donor of a crime punishable by imprisonment of at least three years, unless the false accusation is prosecuted on the victim's complaint and none was filed; and
c) refuses to give the donor support that the donor needs.
These rules do not apply to customary and remunerative gifts.
The claim may be brought within one year of the donor learning of the grounds for revocation. Until this term expires, the donor's heirs may also bring it if the donor died before that.
A waiver of this claim made in advance is void.
The revocation does not affect the rights acquired by third persons in the donated properties before the note of the claim, but the recipient owes the donor compensation for what he was enriched by.
Art. 228. By a lease contract the landlord undertakes to provide the tenant with a thing for temporary use, and the tenant undertakes to pay a set rent.
Art. 237. On the transfer of real estate, the lease contract remains in force towards the acquirer if it was entered in the property register.

A lease concluded before the transfer, if it has a certain date, binds the acquirer until the agreed term, but not for more than one year from the transfer. If it has no certain date and the tenant is in possession, it binds the acquirer as a lease without a fixed term.
The landlord owes the tenant compensation if the tenant loses the use of the property before the end of the lease because of the transfer.

Art. 240. By a loan contract the lender transfers to the borrower the ownership of money or other fungible things, and the borrower undertakes to return the sum or things of the same kind, quantity and quality.
The borrower owes interest only if agreed in writing. This does not apply to banks.
Art. 247 applies to the loan.
Unless agreed otherwise, the borrower must return the money or things within one month of being asked.
